mainTopic: Moving a bed (מטה) on Shabbat that has or had money (מעות) on it: the corrected version of רב's ruling, and the role of בין השמשות and מוקצה
overview: This amud opens at the end of an objection to an earlier version of רב's ruling about a bed (מטה) set aside for money (מעות). The challenger argues with a קל וחומר: an unlit lamp (נר) may be moved, so a bed that never had money placed on it surely may be moved too. The גמרא therefore restates רב's ruling in corrected form. A bed designated for money becomes forbidden only once money was actually placed on it. A bed that was not designated is forbidden only while money is on it, provided the money was not on it during בין השמשות. עולא then reports an objection by רבי אליעזר from a משנה about a wagon's undercarriage (מוכני). That משנה implies the wagon is permitted once the money is gone, even if money was on it during בין השמשות. The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה, while רב follows רבי יהודה, who does.

steps.title: A lamp proves that a bed should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: The challenger finishes his objection to the earlier version of רב's ruling with a קל וחומר from an unlit lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lamp is made for lighting, yet if it was not lit, it may be moved on Shabbat. A bed is not made for holding money, so surely it may be moved if no money was put on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an attack on the earlier version of רב's ruling, which said a bed designated for money is forbidden even with no money on it. The attack is a קל וחומר from a נר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamp's whole purpose is to hold a forbidden flame, yet an unlit lamp is not מוקצה. A bed's main purpose is sleeping, not holding money. So merely designating a bed for money, without putting money on it, cannot be stricter than an unused lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (a fortiori)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an objection that began on the previous amud. The challenger is not arguing that money makes no difference. He argues only that designation alone, with no money ever placed, cannot forbid the bed.

phrases.english: And just as a lamp, which is made for this purpose (lighting),
when he did not light it,
it is permitted to move it,
a bed, which is not made for this purpose (holding money),
all the more so (it should be permitted)?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection begun on the previous amud against the original version of רב's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רב's ruling that a bed designated for money is forbidden even without money on it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: an unlit lamp, made for a forbidden use, may be moved, so a bed not primarily made for money surely may be moved when no money was placed on it

steps.title: Corrected version of רב: a bed designated for money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב's ruling: a designated bed becomes forbidden only after money was actually placed on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רב said it, this is what he said: if a bed was designated for money and money was put on it, it may not be moved. If money was never put on it, it may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the lamp objection, the גמרא rewrites what רב actually said, starting with the case of a bed designated for money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Designation alone does nothing, which fits the lamp argument. Once designation is combined with actually placing money on the bed, the bed takes on a forbidden status. From then on it may not be moved even when the money is not on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: 'He placed money on it' here means money was placed at some point after the designation, not necessarily on Shabbat. Once that happens, the bed is forbidden even if it is empty now.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated as follows:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A bed that one designated for money,
if he placed money on it,
it is forbidden to move it;
if he did not place money on it,
it is permitted to move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the lamp objection by reformulating רב's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reformulation of the original statement (אי איתמר הכי איתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב forbade a designated bed even with no money ever placed on it
steps.terutzMaskana: A designated bed is forbidden only once money was actually placed on it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Designation plus actual placement of money makes the bed forbidden; designation alone does not

steps.title: A bed not designated for money, and the twilight condition
steps.stepSummary: A bed that was not designated is forbidden only while money is on it, provided the money was not there during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bed was not designated for money: when money is on it, it may not be moved. When no money is on it, it may be moved. This applies only if money was not on it during twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: The corrected ruling of רב continues with the second case: an ordinary bed that just happens to have money on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an undesignated bed, the forbidden status depends on whether money is on it now. There is one catch. If money was on it during בין השמשות, the moment Shabbat began, the bed is set aside (מוקצה) for the whole Shabbat, even after the money is removed.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the moment Shabbat begins, which sets an object's status for all of Shabbat

steps.whatToRemember: Designated bed: forbidden once money was ever placed on it. Undesignated bed: forbidden only while money is on it, unless the money was there at בין השמשות. In that case it stays forbidden all Shabbat.
steps.whyThisMatters: The condition about בין השמשות is exactly what the next objection attacks. It shows that רב holds a status fixed at twilight lasts the whole day.

phrases.english: If he did not designate it for money:
if there is money on it, it is forbidden to move it;
if there is no money on it, it is permitted to move it.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עָלֶיהָ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: And that is provided that (money) was not on it during twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reformulated statement of רב with the undesignated case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An undesignated bed is forbidden only while money is on it, unless money was on it at בין השמשות, in which case it stays forbidden all Shabbat

steps.title: Objection from the wagon's undercarriage
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that רבי אליעזר challenged רב from a משנה about a wagon's detachable undercarriage (מוכני).
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: רבי אליעזר objected from this משנה: a wagon's undercarriage, when it can be detached, is not counted as connected to the wagon. It is not measured together with it, and it does not protect along with it in a tent over a dead body. And one may not drag the wagon on Shabbat when there is money on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to set up an objection against רב. The actual point of the objection comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of this משנה deals with טומאה laws, treating a detachable undercarriage as separate from the wagon. The part relevant to us is the last clause: the wagon may not be dragged on Shabbat 'when there is money on it.' The problem lies in what that wording implies.

keyTerms.meaning: The undercarriage or wheel-base of a wagon
A tent or covering over a dead body (טומאה law)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the טומאה details of this משנה. For this סוגיא, only the final clause about Shabbat and money matters.

phrases.english: Ulla said: Rabbi Eliezer raised an objection:
Its (the wagon's) undercarriage, when it is detachable,
is not considered connected to it,
and is not measured together with it,
and does not protect together with it in a tent over a corpse,
and one may not drag it on Shabbat
when there is money on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a תנאי source to challenge the twilight condition in רב's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's condition that an object holding money at בין השמשות stays forbidden all Shabbat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set-up: the משנה ties the prohibition only to money being on the wagon 'at that time'; the inference is drawn in the next step

steps.title: The inference: no money now means permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference from the משנה: once the money is gone, the wagon is permitted, even if money was on it at בין השמשות. This contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if there is no money on it, it is permitted, even though money was on it during twilight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the punch of the objection. The משנה's wording suggests the twilight status does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids dragging the wagon only 'when there is money on it,' which suggests that once the money is removed, it is allowed. That directly clashes with רב, who said money present at בין השמשות keeps the object forbidden for the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (introducing an inference from wording)

phrases.english: This implies: if there is no money on it, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ עָלֶיהָ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת!
phrases.english: even though (money) was on it during twilight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection set up by quoting the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that money present at בין השמשות forbids the object all Shabbat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inference from the משנה's wording 'when there is money on it': without money now, it is permitted regardless of twilight status

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון; רב follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה, while רב follows רבי יהודה, who does.
steps.simpleTranslation: That משנה follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה. רב holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing that the משנה and רב follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rejects the idea that an object becomes set aside for the whole day because of its status at twilight, so for him only the present matters. רבי יהודה accepts מוקצה, so an object set aside at בין השמשות stays forbidden all Shabbat. רב sides with רבי יהודה, so the משנה is no contradiction to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside: an item excluded from use on Shabbat

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over whether a twilight status lasts all Shabbat comes down to מוקצה. רבי שמעון does not hold of it, while רבי יהודה does. רב follows רבי יהודה, so money present at בין השמשות keeps the bed forbidden all day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רב's practical ruling about beds and money to the larger מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on מוקצה, which runs throughout this פרק.

phrases.english: That (mishna) is (the view of) Rabbi Shimon,
who does not hold of (the prohibition of) set-aside;
and Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection from the wagon משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different תנא (תנאי dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that twilight status is irrelevant, contradicting רב
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who rejects מוקצה; רב follows רבי יהודה, who accepts it, so there is no contradiction
